steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Latin nouns change their endings to show their grammatical function in a sentence; this system is called declension. | Key Fact: There are five declensions, each with a characteristic vowel in the stem: 1st (a-stem), 2nd (o-stem), 3rd (consonant/i-stem), 4th (u-stem), 5th (e-stem). | Key Fact: Every Latin noun has a gender: masculine, feminine, or neuter. Gender must be learned with each noun and does not always match natural sex. | Key Fact: First declension nouns are mostly feminine (e.g. puella, villa, familia). Exceptions like nauta and agricola are masculine.

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on key terms from nouns & declensions, and one past-paper question.
